Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Most common malocclusion found in people is:
Explanation: [M.S.RANI 3rd ed 22] The type of malocclusion most common among the population is crowded teeth (Class I with incisor crowding).

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: The six keys to normal occlusion was introduced by:
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3rd ed 59] According to Andrews, the six keys to normal occlusion are: Molar inter-arch relationship, Mesio-distal crown angulation, Labio-lingual crown angulation, Absence of rotation, Tight contacts, Curve of spee.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: The role of antiflux in soldering stainless steel is
Option A: To remove the chromium oxide layer
Option B: To increase the flow of solder
Option C: To reduce the fusion temperature of solder
Option D: To limit the flow of solder
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3rd ed. 474] Antiflux is used to confine the flow of molten solder to the metals being joined.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Which of following is used as antiflux
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3rd ed 474] The commonly used antiflux are lead pencil markings, graphite lines.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Flux used in stainless steel solder are all except
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3rd ed 474] The flux commonly used in dentistry consists of: Borax glass-55%, Boric acid-35%, Silica-10%. Fluoride fluxes contain Boric acid and potassium fluoride. Sodium fluoride is not.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: E.H. Angle introduced his classification of malocclusions
Explanation: [Bhalaji 5th ed 87] Line of occlusion described by Edward angle (1899).

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: The line passing through the cingulum of the anterior teeth and central fossa of the posterior teeth is
Explanation: [Orthodontics prep manual by Sridhar Premkumar Pg 120] Line of occlusion described by Edward angle: Maxillary: Smooth, parabolic curve passing through the central fossa of each upper molar and along the cingulum of upper canines and incisors.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Prolonged thumb sucking directly results in all of the following Except
Explanation: Thumb sucking leads to anterior open bite, not deep over bite.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Which of the following is the only posterior dental cross bite?
Option A: Maxillary anterior alveolus is overlapped by mandibular anterior alveolus
Option B: Mandibular posterior jaw segment is displaced to overlap maxillary posterior jaw segment
Option C: Maxillary posterior dental segment is overlapped by the mandibular posterior teeth
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3rd ed 423-425] Posterior crossbite is due to abnormal transverse relationship between the upper and lower posterior teeth. Mandibular cusps occlude buccal to the maxillary buccal cusps (Maxillary posterior dental segment is overlapped by the mandibular posterior teeth).

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: All of the following are dental characteristics of a skeletal class III malocclusion, except:
Explanation: [M.S. Rani 3rd ed 22] Distrocclusion is synonymous with skeletal class II malocclusion.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Which of the following is a feature of Class I type 3 malocclusion?
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3rd ed 76] Type 3: Class I with anterior cross bite.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Malocclusion representing a transverse deficiency is often referred to as:
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3 ed 67] Transverse malocclusion involves Crossbite, buccal non occlusion, lingual non occlusion.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Thumb sucking is normal upto:
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3 ed 97] Thumb sucking is normal up to 3-4 years.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: The tooth that is used to identify the type of class universally is:
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3 ed 69] Angle based his classifications on the relative position of the permanent Maxillary First Molar.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Curve of occlusion touching the buccal and lingual surfaces of mandibular buccal cusoal teeth is called
Explanation: [Bhalajhi 3 ed 56, 57] The curve of Wilson is medio-lateral on each side of arch and it results from inward inclination of lower posterior teeth. It contacts the buccal and lingual cusp tips of the mandibular buccal teeth.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Which of the following is most common trigger for BRUXISM?
Option C: Discrepancy between centric relation and centric occlusion
Explanation: Occlusal discrepancies are a major trigger for bruxism. Discrepancy between centric relation and centric occlusion.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Vertical malocclusions include
Explanation: Vertical anomalies include Deep bite, open bite. Deep overbite anomalies are categorized into: Dentally supported and Gingivally supported.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Decreased collum angle is seen in
Explanation: [Orthodontics by Om Prakash 1st ed Pg 396] The angle formed by the intersection of the long axes of the crown and root angulation or collum angle. It is decreased in Class II Div 2 cases.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Which of the following is not a self-correcting anomaly In a 9 year old child?
Explanation: [Orthodontic diagnosis by Thomas Rakosi and Thomas Gaber Pg 451] Anterior open bite is not self-correcting orthodontic problem. It has to be intercepted and treated early.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: First to classify malocclusion on structural basis?
Explanation: [Gurukeerat Sing 2nd ed 170] Salzamen in 1950 was the first to classify malocclusion based on skeletal structures.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: When does a child's chewing pattern typically transition to that of an adult?
Option A: With the eruption of permanent first molars
Option B: With the establishment of mixed dentition
Option C: After the eruption of permanent canines
Option D: With the loss of deciduous second molars
Explanation: [Proffit 6th ed 65] The transition from the juvenile to the adult chewing pattern develops in conjunction with the eruption of the permanent canines at about age 12.

Subject: Orthodontics
Question: Which of the following is the most common type of malocclusion associated with a Class Il skeletal relationship?
Explanation: A Class II skeletal relationship is commonly characterized by either a forward position of the maxilla, a retruded mandible, or a combination of both. This skeletal discrepancy often manifests as an increased overjet.
